_README: Free, official consolidated designation lists. Used by BOTH scripts/sanctions-watch.mjs (fingerprints each list for changes) AND scripts/sanctions-screen.mjs (screens the Asana customer base against them — no external engine, no API key). Each source: id, name, jurisdiction, url, type (csv|xml), `parser` (ofac|un|ofsi|eu|xml — which extractor sanctions-match.mjs uses), optional marker (a substring counted once per record for an approximate entry-count delta). Additional / curated lists (UAE EOCN, extra national XML lists) live in data/sanctions-extra.json.

sources.name: US OFAC — SDN a.k.a. list (alt.csv)
sources._note: The SDN's weak/strong a.k.a. names live in this SEPARATE headerless file (ent_num, alt_num, alt_type, alt_name, remarks). The screen folds them into the primary OFAC SDN list (mergeInto) so an alias hit reads as the SDN designation it is — screening sdn.csv's primary names alone is a false-negative gap (a party operating under an SDN alias would screen clear; mirrors screen.py parse_ofac_alt). If this file fails to load, the primary SDN list still screens but is flagged partial: alias coverage missing, standing SDN matches carried forward, never cleared off reduced coverage. COVERAGE FLOOR: minNames is PROVISIONAL and deliberately well below the observed a.k.a. count — it exists to catch a truncated body or a column shift (which would yield hundreds, not thousands), not to police normal churn. Ratchet it toward ~50% of the observed baseline once runs have logged real counts, per the floors-only-rise convention.

sources.name: UK OFSI — Consolidated list of targets (CSV)

_README_minNames: minNames: per-source coverage floor. A list parsing below it is a truncated download / parser drift, not a mass de-listing: it still screens (hits are real) but is marked partial (standing matches carried, not cleared) and the run reports DEGRADED. Mirrors screen.py CORE_LIST_FLOORS (~50% of verified baselines). Alias files (mergeInto) carry a floor TOO. They were exempted on the theory that the fold's partial machinery covered them, but that machinery only handles a TOTALLY ABSENT alias file — a truncated-but-nonzero one folded in as full coverage, and because alias hits are recorded under the PRIMARY list name, an alias-derived standing match then cleared as if re-verified.
